claims.text: An active learning–based machine-learning framework can integrate existing simulation and experimental data for RHEA design.
The active-learning framework can rapidly predict composition–property relationships for RHEAs.
The framework can identify RHEA compositions that simultaneously provide intrinsic strength, ductility, and low weight.
RHEAs typically comprise multiple principal elements in a BCC solid solution.
Such RHEAs are typically produced by arc melting or spark plasma sintering.
Incorporating newly generated simulation and experimental data iteratively refines the model's predictions.
BCC-phase stability and controlled local lattice distortions mediate dislocation motion in the proposed alloys.
The framework learns correlations between composition and strength, ductility, and density from thermo-kinetic and simulation datasets.
Selecting new experiments to maximize information gain narrows the compositional search toward candidates satisfying all desired properties.
HEAs have a vast compositional design space that requires efficient exploration tools.
Computational alloy-design methods can rapidly screen thousands of HEA compositions and reduce them to a small set of candidates.
The proposed active-learning method will reduce RHEA exploration time relative to exhaustive simulations or experiments.
Traditional thermo-kinetic analyses and case-by-case simulations are time-intensive and combinatorially expensive.
The proposed strategy may not extend directly from RHEAs to non-refractory alloys or non-HEA systems.
The strategy's success depends on the quality and representativeness of the experimental and simulation database.
Sparse training data may make the machine-learning predictions less reliable.
